problem: A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with acceleration $a(t)=1-6t,$ where $t\ge 0$ is the time. If the particle has position $x=2$ and velocity $v=4$ when $t=0,$ calculate the position $x$ of the particle at time $t>0.$
worked_solution:
We start by integrating the acceleration to get the velocity $v(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int (1-6t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =t-3{t}^{2}+C\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C,$ we use the fact that $v(0)=4.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}4 & =(0)-3(0)^{2}+C \\ C & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

So the velocity is given by $v(t)=t-3{t}^{2}+4.$

Now, we integrate the velocity to get $x(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & =\int v(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int (t-3{t}^{2}+4)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{t}^{2}-{t}^{3}+4t+K\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $K,$ we use the fact that $x(0)=2.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}2 & =\frac{1}{2}(0)^{2}-(0)^{3}+4(0)+K \\ K & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the position $x$ of the particle at time $t$ is 

$$
x(t)=\frac{1}{2}{t}^{2}-{t}^{3}+4t+2.
$$
